## Frozen literals and the anchoring fix

Round-1 review BLOCKed with one finding. It is **correct**, and sweeping the same ground turned up a **second** defect it missed. Both are now fixed in AC1.

### B1 (reviewer, CORRECT) — an unrecorded frozen literal

`tests/fixtures/dc_wiki_corpus/code_arrow.json:16` contains `test_gate_error_sidecar_heldout.py`, and it is neither `.test_durations` nor the `.github/mechanism-baseline.json` row — the only two exclusions AC1 named. AC1's escape clause permits "any frozen pre-fix literal explicitly recorded on this ticket," and this literal was not recorded. The reviewer caught exactly that.

**Recording it now.** The file is a frozen Data Center wiki-render corpus built by `scripts/build_dc_wiki_corpus.py`; the hit sits inside a captured `/rebar-debug` report body stored verbatim as render input. Editing it would corrupt the fixture's purpose, which is to reproduce real DC wiki render inputs byte-for-byte. It is the same class as `.test_durations`: generated, frozen, not a code reference. AC1 now names it explicitly.

### B2 (missed by the review) — AC1's recipe contradicted AC1's own text

AC1 ended with "each hit attributed to its owning path rather than matched as a substring," but prescribed a bare `git grep -F <basename>`, which does nothing of the kind.

`test_registry_heldout.py` is a literal substring of `test_attest_registry_heldout.py`, starting at index 7 and preceded by a word character:

```
test_attest_registry_heldout.py
       ^-- test_registry_heldout.py starts here
```

S1 `361f` merged that pair and left the source named in two provenance comments, `tests/unit/test_attest_registry.py:14` and `:84`. So after this story deletes `tests/unit/metrics/test_registry_heldout.py`, the unanchored grep still returns 2 hits — permanently, in a file this story does not touch and must not touch. No implementation could have cleared them, so AC1 would have failed at the end regardless of the work. Same failure class as the `new=0` mechanism-delta AC amended across this epic earlier today.

**Fix:** `git grep -nE "(^|[^A-Za-z0-9_])<basename>"`. Measured on `bd793558957`: anchored returns **0** hits for `test_registry_heldout.py` (down from 2) and still returns the genuine `code_arrow.json:16` hit for `test_gate_error_sidecar_heldout.py`, so it suppresses only the superstring class.

### Full live-reference census for all 22 basenames at `bd793558957`

| Referencing path | Hits | Disposition |
|---|---|---|
| `.test_durations` | 140 | excluded (generated) |
| `.github/mechanism-baseline.json:61` | 1 | excluded (stale row, named in Testing) |
| `tests/fixtures/dc_wiki_corpus/code_arrow.json:16` | 1 | excluded (frozen corpus; recorded here) |
| `tests/unit/test_attest_registry.py:14,:84` | 2 | **not a reference** — substring artifact; 0 under anchoring |

### Pre-sweep of the rest of the plan, at `bd793558957`

Pair census confirms **22** exactly: 13 `tests/unit/metrics/` + 3 `tests/unit/workflow/` + 6 across the `tests/unit/reconciler/` tree (1 root, 2 `diffing/`, 3 `state/`). The `_clean` autouse cite `tests/unit/reconciler/state/test_backend_scalar_surface{,_heldout}.py::_clean` resolves exactly. S1's merge touched no file in this stratum, so no before-count recorded in the plan has drifted.

### The attribution rule AC1's sweep requires

AC1's grep, run naively, also reports 45 hits that are **this change's own provenance records**: the merged docstring line `Held-out oracles merged from <name>_heldout.py: …` and the mandated divider `# ── held-out oracles (merged from <name>_heldout.py) ──`, each sitting in the very base module that absorbed that twin.

The Testing section states the rule directly: "Attribute every hit to its owning path before acting on it."

So the sweep is run as: for basename `X_heldout.py`, exclude hits inside `X.py`, the base module that owns that provenance. Everything else must fall in the exception set. Measured that way the sweep returns **exactly the 2 rows above and nothing else**.

Without that rule AC1 and the Approach contradict each other: the Approach *mandates* a divider naming the deleted file, so no conforming implementation could ever return zero hits.

- 22 pairs merged; **380** top-level definitions in, **380** out (195 base + 236 held − 51 identical dedupes), zero mismatches.
- **14 renames over 7 pairs**, matching the plan's enumerated set name for name, including `test_canonical_link_diff` correctly carrying **0** renames as the plan's correction states.

### One mechanical hazard worth recording

Renaming lengthened 2 lines in `test_canonical_outbound_equivalence.py` past the 100-character limit (`_jira` → `_jira_heldout` adds 8 characters per call), so `ruff check --fix` left 7 E501 errors that only `ruff format` could resolve. comments.body:
AC5 contradiction — measured, and the evidence AC5 now points at.

`make verify` failed with exactly **1 failure out of 20,135 tests** (rc=2, 1h20m):

    tests/unit/test_mechanism_delta.py::test_the_committed_baseline_matches_the_live_tree

The extra item is one baseline row:

    autouse_fixture::tests/unit/reconciler/state/test_backend_scalar_surface_heldout.py::_clean

That names a file this story deletes, so the row cannot survive the merge.

**Why AC5 as written could not be satisfied.** `scripts/check_mechanism_delta.py --check` buckets the row `stale` and exits 0 — `active=647 new=28 increased=0 stale=1`. AC5's first clause therefore passed. But `make verify` runs a second, stricter gate the plan never accounted for: the pytest test above asserts `set(baseline) | admitted == live` **exactly**, with no tolerance for a stale row. So AC5 ("`--update-stale` is not run") and AC6 ("`make verify` green") were mutually unsatisfiable. No implementation could have met both.

**What the drain does.** `python scripts/check_mechanism_delta.py --update-stale` removes **exactly 1 row** — the one above, nothing else. Afterwards `stale` goes 1 → 0, `--check` still exits 0, and all **33** tests in `tests/unit/test_mechanism_delta.py` pass.

**The mechanism is not being removed — the row is a duplicate.** This is the part worth recording, because "a drained baseline row" normally means a mechanism disappeared. It did not here. The surviving twin `tests/unit/reconciler/state/test_backend_scalar_surface.py:27-28` still declares its own `_clean` autouse fixture, and the baseline already carries a row for it at line 60. The two modules each declared an identical fixture; merging them deduplicated the declaration. The census count drops by one because one of two identical declarations went away, not because the mechanism did.

**Why the drain is the sanctioned path, not a workaround.** `AGENTS.md` is explicit for this exact case: "When your own change removes a mechanism, run `python scripts/check_mechanism_delta.py --update-stale` in that change and commit the shrunken baseline." It equally forbids the alternative: "Do **not** hand-edit `.github/mechanism-baseline.json`." The drain also cannot launder a regression — it "refuses while any unadmitted mechanism is new or increased," which is why it is a ratchet rather than a freeze.

So the previous AC5 wording forbade the one path the repository's own guidance requires. AC5 is amended to require the drain; the diff is 1 deleted line in `.github/mechanism-baseline.json`.

**Pattern note.** This is the second AC-versus-reality defect in this family, both in the same gate. The first was `new=0` (amended earlier; root cause bug `6f24-3d47-b251-4905`). Both came from reasoning about `--check`'s summary rather than running the gate the CI contract actually runs. The general lesson, which applies beyond this story: `check_mechanism_delta.py --check` exiting 0 is **not** the whole mechanism gate, and a plan that cites only `--check` will pass `make lint` and fail `make verify` 80 minutes later.

`pytest tests/unit/test_mechanism_delta.py` is **not** reported separately here on purpose: `make verify` runs it, and running it concurrently against this worktree while the verify is mid-flight would contend for the same tree. Its result arrives with AC6 rather than as a second, weaker measurement.

Run at `693030cb9ab8b961cd1586a056f2d3ea1741989e`, worktree clean, in `.rebar/scratch/verify-19c3/`. Zero failures, zero errors.

That closes the last open criterion. ACs 1–5 were verified and filed earlier on this ticket; AC6 is the one that could only be answered by the full run, and it answers clean.

**Pushed as Gerrit change [3194](https://rebar.solutions.navateam.com/c/rebar/+/3194)**, tagged `rebar-session-6a3fecbb-7c5e-4e07-b1ba-7eb2bd09cb7c`. Awaiting `LLM-Review +1` and `Verified +1` before submit; this ticket closes only after the change merges.

### One cross-check worth recording, because it nearly produced a false defect report

The AC1 sweep is word-anchored for a reason this run re-confirmed. A bare `git grep -F test_registry_heldout.py` reports a hit inside the **live** file `tests/unit/test_attest_registry.py` — which reads as a dangling reference to a module this story deleted. It is not. `attest` ends in `test`, so `test_attest_registry_heldout.py` contains `test_registry_heldout.py` as a substring starting at index 7. The anchored form `git grep -nE "(^|[^A-Za-z0-9_])<basename>"` returns 0 for that basename while still catching the genuine `code_arrow.json:16` literal.

This is the exact failure mode the AC1 amendment was written to prevent, encountered independently while verifying the amendment. The anchoring is load-bearing, not cosmetic.

Separately, the `.github/mechanism-baseline.json` stale row that AC1 permits as an exemption produced **no** hit, because the `--update-stale` drain required by AC5 removed it in this same commit. The exemption is now unused — correctly so, and harmless to leave in the AC text.

## Context / Problem
22 modules under `tests/unit/metrics/` (13 pairs), `tests/unit/workflow/` (3 pairs) and `tests/unit/reconciler/` (6 pairs: 2 in `diffing/`, 3 in `state/`, 1 at the package root) have a `<name>_heldout.py` twin. Once both oracles have been reviewed the split only doubles module count, duplicates identical helper definitions, and makes every rename touch two files. Across these 22 pairs no test-function name collides; 7 pairs carry helper/fixture/class definitions with differing bodies (14 definitions in all) and every other colliding definition is identical. The pair list with per-pair rename sets, filtered from enumeration (2) of the test-suite epic's first comment, is itemised in this ticket's first comment. Paths are stated at their post-rename name: the reconciler epic (friended-brainsick-degus) rename has LANDED, so `tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/` no longer exists and the modules live under `tests/unit/reconciler/`. All counts and paths in this plan were re-measured on origin/main ce5795c6a5c by listing `tests/unit/{metrics,workflow,reconciler}/` and AST-diffing every pair's top-level definitions, not sampled.

## Approach
Directories: `tests/unit/metrics/`, `tests/unit/workflow/`, `tests/unit/reconciler/` — 22 pairs (13 metrics, 3 workflow, 6 reconciler — 2 in `diffing/`, 3 in `state/`, 1 at the package root). **14 definition renames over 7 pairs**, enumerated so the set does not have to be re-derived: `metrics/test_registry` (`_spec`); `metrics/test_event_metrics` (`_write_event`, `_ticket`); `metrics/test_git_metrics` (`_oracle_write_cap`); `metrics/test_sidecar_metrics` (`_review`, `_write`); `workflow/test_gate_error_sidecar` (`_OutageRunner`, `_gate_errors`); `reconciler/state/test_backend_scalar_surface` (`_backend`); `reconciler/diffing/test_canonical_outbound_equivalence` (`_jira`, `backend`, `_emit`, `_StubBindingStore`, `_ticket`). `reconciler/diffing/test_canonical_link_diff` was previously listed as a rename and is NOT one: its shared definitions are byte-identical, so it dedupes with no rename. For each pair: `cat` the held-out module into the base under a `# ── held-out oracles (merged from <name>_heldout.py) ──` divider; keep the base module docstring and append the held-out docstring's "what it proves" paragraph; dedupe identical definitions (`pytestmark` counts here — keep the base copy); rename differing definitions and repoint their callers; `git rm` the held-out file. Rename rule: suffix the HELD-OUT definition `_heldout` (e.g. `_load_heldout`) and repoint its callers; keep the base copy of identical definitions. The autouse fixture `tests/unit/reconciler/state/test_backend_scalar_surface{,_heldout}.py::_clean` has identical bodies: the merge keeps the base copy, so the base mechanism key survives and the held-out key buckets `stale`. No test body changes.

## Scope
In scope: the 22 base modules under `tests/unit/metrics/`, `tests/unit/workflow/` and `tests/unit/reconciler/` named in the first comment and their 22 `_heldout` twins. Out of scope: the `tests/unit/` root pairs (S1), `tests/interfaces/` and `tests/integration/` (S3), `tests/scripts/` (S4), the 78 unpaired held-out renames (S5), every file under `src/`, and any test body change. `.github/mechanism-baseline.json` is in scope for the AC5 drain only.

`tests/unit/review_bot/` was flagged as possibly unclaimed by any story in this epic. It is not: all 3 of its `_heldout` modules are **unpaired**, so they belong to `b721-6c6d`'s unpaired-rename pass, whose scope claims the 55 unpaired modules under `tests/unit/` *including its subpackages*. Nothing is added to this story.

## Testing
**Whole-tree deleted-filename sweep, before `make test`.** For each of the 22 removed `_heldout.py` basenames, `git grep -F <basename>` over the whole tree and classify every hit as a live reference (fix), stale prose (fix), or a frozen pre-fix literal (leave, and record it on this ticket). Sweeping only the merged pair is demonstrably insufficient: sibling story 361f-0a5c-bd12-463b broke four guard modules it never edited — a `parametrize` list, a nested-pytest node id, an AST-scan target path and a vocabulary allowlist entry — and its earlier pair-scoped run passed because a merged module never cites a sibling's path.

Measured on origin/main ce5795c6a5c, the live set for this directory set is **exactly one** hit: the `.github/mechanism-baseline.json` row `autouse_fixture::tests/unit/reconciler/state/test_backend_scalar_surface_heldout.py::_clean`, which the Approach covers and which the AC5 drain removes (the two `_clean` fixtures are byte-identical, so dedupe keeps the already-pinned base copy and the twin's key buckets `stale`). `scripts/criteria-vocabulary-allowlist.txt` pins none of these 22 paths, so this story does not touch it.

**Match on the whole basename, not a substring.** A bare `git grep -F` over basenames over-reports: `test_attest_registry_heldout.py` contains `test_registry_heldout.py`, so twin `test_registry_heldout.py` appears to own a docstring reference in `tests/unit/test_attest_registry.py` that is in fact sibling 361f's to fix. Attribute every hit to its owning path before acting on it. `.test_durations` hits are excluded: it is a pytest-split sharding profile, tolerant of stale keys and exempt from the vocabulary gate, confirmed by 361f deleting 39 modules keyed in it with no resulting failure.

Per pair: `pytest --collect-only -q <base> <heldout>` before and `pytest --collect-only -q <base>` after — counts equal (both recorded on this ticket); `pytest <base>` green. `make test` green.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [x] No deleted filename is still referenced: for each of the 22 removed `_heldout.py` basenames, the WORD-ANCHORED `git grep -nE "(^|[^A-Za-z0-9_])<basename>"` returns no hit outside `.test_durations`, the `.github/mechanism-baseline.json` stale row named in Testing, and the one frozen literal recorded in the "Frozen literals and the anchoring fix" comment on this ticket (`tests/fixtures/dc_wiki_corpus/code_arrow.json:16`). **AMENDED 2026-10-31 — the original bare `git grep -F <basename>` could not satisfy this AC's own "rather than matched as a substring" clause.** `test_registry_heldout.py` is a literal substring of `test_attest_registry_heldout.py` (at index 7), which S1 `361f` left named in the provenance comments at `tests/unit/test_attest_registry.py:14,:84`, so the unanchored grep reports 2 permanent false hits that no implementation of this story could clear. Anchoring returns 0 for that basename while still finding the genuine `code_arrow.json` hit.
- [x] `python scripts/check_mechanism_delta.py --check` **exits 0** and `python scripts/check_criteria_vocabulary.py` **exits 0**.
- [x] Zero paired twins remain in these directories: for each of the 22 pairs `git ls-files <base>_heldout.py` prints nothing (the unpaired `_heldout` modules in these directories are untouched here and renamed in S5).
- [x] Per-pair node counts reconcile: each merged base collects exactly the sum of the two prior counts, from the before/after `pytest --collect-only -q` runs recorded on this ticket.
- [x] `python scripts/check_mechanism_delta.py --check` **exits 0** AND `pytest tests/unit/test_mechanism_delta.py` passes, with the stale `_clean` autouse row for the deleted `test_backend_scalar_surface_heldout.py` drained by `python scripts/check_mechanism_delta.py --update-stale` and the shrunken baseline committed here. **AMENDED 2026-10-31 (2nd): the prior wording forbade `--update-stale`, contradicting this story's own `make verify` criterion.** `--check` tolerates a `stale` row, but `make verify` also runs `test_the_committed_baseline_matches_the_live_tree`, asserting `set(baseline) | admitted == live` exactly. `AGENTS.md` prescribes this drain and forbids hand-editing the baseline. Evidence: the "AC5 contradiction" comment. The earlier `new=0` amendment stands (bug `6f24-3d47-b251-4905`).
- [x] `make verify` green.
